items.title: Tolliver interviewed by Monk Rowe, 2021
items.q: a lot of the artists, they delved into that, you know, with the music, you know, Charles Mingus and others, Max Roach you know.

ctx.x: It just occurred to me that 1964 is a significant year for you, it was also the Civil Rights Bill of 1964, and if you extrapolate on that, was the situation socially and politically at that time, do you feel it affected the change in jazz that you’re describing?

Well I think that the development of the jazz art form would have happened the way it did even if the social and political developments didn’t happen around that same time. But of course a lot of the artists, they delved into that, you know, with the music, you know, Charles Mingus and others, Max Roach you know. But honestly, although I was paying close attention to what was going on socially and politically, I didn’t write or play my music with that in mind. Now it might be hard for folks to believe that didn’t…
Is it safe to say you were obsessed with it?
